title: Retrieval Augmented Generation for LLMs: A Survey
methodology: Systematic literature review of RAG architectures across 100+ papers
findings: RAG significantly reduces hallucination in open-domain QA
Dense retrieval outperforms sparse retrieval on most benchmarks
Chunk size has significant impact on retrieval quality
claims: RAG is more cost-effective than fine-tuning for knowledge-intensive tasks
Hybrid retrieval combining dense and sparse methods yields best results
limitations: Most evaluations are on English-only datasets
Latency overhead of retrieval not benchmarked consistently
No unified evaluation framework across studies

title: Agentic RAG: A Survey
methodology: Taxonomy-based review of agentic RAG systems with multi-step reasoning
findings: Agentic RAG outperforms naive RAG on multi-hop reasoning tasks
Most agentic systems lack robust error recovery mechanisms
claims: Future RAG systems will require planning and self-reflection capabilities
Single-step retrieval is insufficient for complex queries
limitations: Evaluation benchmarks do not capture multi-step reasoning well
No cross-paper comparison of agentic architectures

title: TeaRAG: Token Efficient Agentic RAG
methodology: Token-budget-aware retrieval framework evaluated on QA benchmarks
findings: Token efficiency can be improved by 40% without accuracy loss
Selective chunk retrieval reduces noise in context window
claims: Token cost is a primary bottleneck in production RAG systems
